target.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying
target.body:
## Summary

Upgrades `llm_input` and `llm_output` plugin hooks from fire-and-forget (void) to sequential modifying hooks. Replaces the closed #61485 with a clean implementation against current `main`.

- `llm_input` handlers can now return `{ block, blockReason, prompt, systemPrompt }` to block or modify the LLM call
- `llm_output` handlers can now return `{ assistantTexts }` to replace the model response (e.g. for redaction)
- Handlers returning `void` behave identically to before (fully backward compatible)

### Mutation semantics

**llm_input:**
- `prompt` / `systemPrompt`: first-setter-wins across priority-ordered handlers
- `block` / `blockReason`: sticky-true (any handler blocks; `shouldStop` exits early)
- Subject to `allowPromptInjection` policy — prompt fields stripped when `false`
- `evolveEvent` propagates the **accumulated merged result** (not raw handler result) to lower-priority handlers and resets `imagesCount` to 0

**llm_output:**
- `assistantTexts`: last-setter-wins with evolved event propagation
- Later hooks see prior modifications, preventing silent overwrites of higher-priority redactions

### Security boundaries

- `PluginBlockedError` sentinel skips failover/retry classification (not a transient provider failure)
- `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook` strips `prompt`/`systemPrompt` from results when `allowPromptInjection=false`
- `historyMessages` deep-cloned via `cloneHookMessages` before passing to hooks
- `lastAssistant` deep-cloned via `structuredClone` before passing to `llm_output` hooks
- `systemPrompt` override applied to active model session via `setActiveSessionSystemPrompt`

### Cross-runner contract

- Embedded runner: fully consumes modifying results (block, prompt/systemPrompt override, output replacement)
- Harness helpers (`runAgentHarnessLlmInputHook`/`LlmOutputHook`): upgraded from `void` to `Promise<Result | undefined>` so CLI, Codex app-server, and Copilot runners can consume modifying results
- Backward compatible — existing fire-and-forget callers discard the promise

### Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/plugins/hook-types.ts` | Add `PluginHookLlmInputResult`, `PluginHookLlmOutputResult` types with documented mutation semantics; add `llm_input` to prompt injection hook names; update handler map signatures |
| `src/plugins/hooks.ts` | Add `evolveEvent` to `ModifyingHookPolicy`; wire into `runModifyingHook` using accumulated result; upgrade `runLlmInput`/`runLlmOutput` from `runVoidHook` to `runModifyingHook` |
| `src/plugins/registry.ts` | Add `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook`; handle `llm_input` in prompt injection guard |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` | Add `PluginBlockedError`; await `llm_input`/`llm_output` results; apply prompt/systemPrompt overrides to active session; wire output replacement |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` | Import `PluginBlockedError`; handle with `hook_block` error kind, skip failover |
| `src/agents/harness/lifecycle-hook-helpers.ts` | Upgrade `runAgentHarnessLlmInputHook`/`LlmOutputHook` to return `Promise<Result>` |
| `src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts` | 18 tests covering block, override, priority merge, A>B>C accumulated-result evolution, backward compat, error handling |

## Verification

- `pnpm test src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts` — 18/18 pass
- `pnpm test src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm.test.ts` — 5/5 pass (backward compat)
- `pnpm tsgo:core` + `pnpm tsgo:extensions` — typecheck clean
- `pnpm lint` — clean
- `pnpm format:check` — clean (our files)
- Merge conflicts resolved against latest `origin/main`

## ClawSweeper P1 findings addressed

All 3 findings from the [initial review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103959#issuecomment-4939779091) (reviewed against `e5b9638`) have been fixed:

1. **evolveEvent uses accumulated result** — `hooks.ts`: `evolveEvent(event, result)` instead of `evolveEvent(event, handlerResult)`. New A>B>C priority test validates.
2. **systemPrompt applied to active session** — `attempt.ts`: `setActiveSessionSystemPrompt()` called after hook override so the model receives the new prompt.
3. **Harness helpers return results** — `lifecycle-hook-helpers.ts`: both functions now return `Promise<Result | undefined>` for cross-runner consumption.

## Supersedes

Replaces #61485 (closed by maintainer as stale)

target.title: fix(agents): restore global subagent model default priority over agent own model
target.body:
## Summary

## Current exact-head refresh

- True-merged upstream `main` snapshot `af1505df659f80893829be5c96e6e9918a9fb42d` into branch head `a2581657124f8f6ca7cd1d861bcbe0280af1a49f`.
- Fresh exact-head GitHub Actions are green: CI, CodeQL, CodeQL Critical Quality, OpenGrep, Workflow Sanity, and iOS Periphery.
- The live resolver proof below was run on the earlier patched head and is retained as prior real-behavior evidence; it was not re-run locally after the merge-only refresh.

Fixes #58822.

- Restores correct subagent model precedence in `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`: global `agents.defaults.subagents.model` now takes priority over the parent agent's own `model.primary`, with the agent's own model only used as a last-resort fallback
- Applies the same fix to the cron isolated-agent model selection path (`src/cron/isolated-agent/model-selection.ts`) and the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper in `src/agents/agent-scope.ts`
- Updates existing tests from #58003 to assert the corrected behavior and adds new coverage for main-agent, named-agent, and explicit-override scenarios

### Background

PR #58003 reordered `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection` to prefer `agentConfig.model` over `agents.defaults.subagents.model`. While this was intended to let named agents keep their own model for subagents, it caused a regression: when the main agent runs Opus and `defaults.subagents.model` is GPT-5.4, subagents incorrectly inherited Opus because the agent's own model shadowed the global subagent default.

The correct precedence is:
1. `agentConfig.subagents.model` — explicit per-agent subagent config (highest)
2. `agents.defaults.subagents.model` — global subagent default
3. `agentConfig.model` — agent's own model (last-resort fallback)

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` — 105 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent.model-formatting.test.ts` — 32 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts` — 11 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/subagent-spawn.model-session.test.ts` — 1 test passes
- [x] `pnpm test src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts` — 84 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` — 34 tests pass
- [x] Test: main agent (Opus) with global subagent default (GPT-5.4) → subagents use GPT-5.4
- [x] Test: named agent without per-agent subagents.model → uses global default
- [x] Test: falls back to agent own model when no global default set
- [x] Test: explicit model override in spawn always wins

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Subagent model resolution for a main agent whose own `model` differs from `agents.defaults.subagents.model`. Before this PR, an Opus-running agent with `defaults.subagents.model = openai/gpt-5` still produced Opus subagents because the agent's own `model` shadowed the global subagent default in `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`, in the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper, and in the cron isolated-agent path. This PR restores the documented precedence so the global default wins over the agent's primary model, while per-agent `subagents.model` still takes the very top slot.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64 (Node v24.15.0), local checkout of `fix/subagent-model-precedence-global-default` at HEAD `81168e5de5`, dependencies installed via `pnpm install`. Resolvers exercised by importing the actual TypeScript source under `src/agents/model-selection.ts` and `src/agents/agent-scope.ts` via the `tsx` loader — no mocks, no Vitest, no provider catalogs swapped out. The cron isolated-agent path uses the same `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper, so the asserted source values cover that resolver too.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
$ cd pr-58823
$ pnpm install --prefer-offline
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/pr-58823-subagent-precedence.mjs
```

The script (`scripts/proof/pr-58823-subagent-precedence.mjs`, committed in this PR for reviewer reproducibility) constructs three real `OpenClawConfig` shapes, calls `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult`, `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`, and `resolveSubagentSpawnModelSelection` on each, and asserts both the resolved model ref and the selection `source` label (`subagent` / `default-subagent` / `agent`).

**Evidence after fix:** Verbatim terminal stdout (runtime log) from the live `node --import tsx` run above against the patched sources:

```

repo head: (local worktree)
node: v24.15.0

--- scenario A — global default beats agent primary ---

input.defaults.subagents.model       = openai/gpt-5

agent-scope raw                      = "openai/gpt-5-mini"
model-selection.resolveConfigured()  = openai/gpt-5-mini
model-selection.resolveSpawn()       = openai/gpt-5-mini
OK scenario B — per-agent override wins

--- scenario C — falls through to agent primary ---

input.defaults.subagents.model       = (unset)
input.agentConfig.subagents.model    = (unset)
agent-scope source                   = agent
agent-scope raw                      = "anthropic/claude-opus"

```

For completeness, the Vitest suites listed in Test plan also pass on this branch (`pnpm test src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` → 105 passed; `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent.model-formatting.test.ts` → 32 passed; etc.), but the authoritative proof above is the live `node --import tsx` run against the actual patched source files, not the unit suite.

**Observed result after fix:**

- Scenario A (Opus main agent, `defaults.subagents.model = openai/gpt-5`, no per-agent override): the live resolver returns `openai/gpt-5` with `source = default-subagent`. Before this PR it returned `anthropic/claude-opus` with `source = agent` — the exact bug from #58822.
- Scenario B (per-agent `subagents.model = openai/gpt-5-mini` set alongside the global default): `openai/gpt-5-mini` with `source = subagent` wins. Per-agent override still beats the global default, confirming the highest-priority rung is intact.
- Scenario C (neither per-agent `subagents.model` nor `defaults.subagents.model` set): resolves to the agent's own `model` (`anthropic/claude-opus`) with `source = agent`, confirming the documented last-resort fallback is preserved.

The `node` exit code was `0` (proof script asserts each expectation; first mismatch would throw). The `agent-scope` source labels are produced by the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper used by both `src/agents/model-selection.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent/model-selection.ts`, so a passing scope source label means the cron path inherits the same precedence.

**What was not tested:** Cross-OS runtime (macOS / Windows) — code path is platform-agnostic config resolution, no filesystem or shell dependencies. Live spawn of an actual subagent process against a remote model provider — the resolver returns the same model ref regardless of whether the downstream spawn succeeds, and the spawn path is exercised by `src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts` (11 passing). Closes #98287
Related: #98234 (non-duplicate reply-session initialization conflict/drop issue)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal users sending quoted replies could have the quoted target extracted into `ReplyToBody` metadata while the agent-facing `BodyForAgent` remained only the new ambiguous message, such as `Did this get done?`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Signal inbound handling now renders visible quoted-reply context directly into `BodyForAgent` as a clear blockquote while preserving clean `RawBody`, `CommandBody`, and `BodyForCommands` for command parsing and hooks. The shared inbound metadata renderer skips only the duplicate one-hop reply-target block when the Signal-generated wrapper exactly matches the expected quoted body and sender; richer `ReplyChain` context and ordinary user-authored blockquotes still render normally.

Signal quoted replies now carry the referenced message into agent-facing input, so agents can answer ambiguous followups using the intended quoted target. Plain non-quoted Signal messages remain unchanged, and quoted context is not duplicated in the model prompt when Signal has already inlined the generated quote block.

target.title: fix(exa): resolve search env secret refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/exa/src/exa-web-search-provider.runtime.ts` read Exa web-search credentials with `readConfiguredSecretString(...) ?? EXA_API_KEY`. That path accepts direct strings, but an env SecretRef in `tools.web.search.exa.apiKey` stays unresolved instead of reading the referenced environment variable.

## Why This Change Was Made

Exa should use the same provider-local credential resolver as the other web-search runtimes: direct config wins, configured env SecretRefs resolve before ambient env fallbacks, and unavailable SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently using `EXA_API_KEY`.

## User Impact

Users can configure Exa web search with an env SecretRef and get the referenced key at runtime without putting the raw key in config. If the referenced env var is missing, the tool reports the normal missing-key state instead of using an unrelated ambient Exa key.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/exa/src/exa-web-search-provider.test.ts`
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/exa/src/exa-web-search-provider.runtime.ts extensions/exa/src/exa-web-search-provider.test.ts`

## Proof

target.title: fix(gateway): keep worker SSH tunnel stderr tails UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Worker SSH tunnel failures retain bounded stdout/stderr diagnostics before `processError()` exposes them to operators. Raw `.slice(-4096)` could begin the retained text on the low half of an emoji or another non-BMP character, producing malformed UTF-16 in the failure message.

This is the production `createWorkerSshRunner()` path used by the worker tunnel manager when SSH exits before its ready marker.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both output streams now share one small `appendBoundedDiagnosticTail` path backed by the repository's canonical `sliceUtf16Safe` helper. The 4096-code-unit cap, redaction, ready-marker behavior, reconnect policy, and success path are unchanged.

The regression invokes the real child-process runner and crosses the exact retention boundary. The maintainer refactor reduced the patch from 53 added lines to 23 while keeping the production boundary under test.

## User Impact

**Before:** A worker SSH failure could show a corrupted leading character when oversized remote output placed a surrogate pair across the retained-tail boundary.

**After:** The incomplete surrogate is discarded and the operator-facing diagnostic remains well-formed.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/gateway/worker-environments/tunnel.ts`
- Regression: `src/gateway/worker-environments/tunnel.test.ts`
- Exact tested head: `f3bfd319b7c1a741976d1cf5f2a24c48858e59f0`

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** worker SSH failure details no longer split UTF-16 surrogate pairs at the bounded stdout/stderr tail.
- **Reachability:** `createWorkerTunnelManager` -> `createWorkerSshRunner().start(...)` -> child output handlers -> `appendBoundedDiagnosticTail` -> `processError(stderr)` -> rejected `ready` promise.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gemini web_search runtime credential resolution treated configured SecretRefs differently from direct string keys. A configured `plugins.entries.google.config.webSearch.apiKey` env SecretRef could be skipped at runtime, allowing the ambient `GEMINI_API_KEY` fallback or the Google model-provider key to be used instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gemini runtime already supports direct plugin search keys, ambient `GEMINI_API_KEY`, and model-provider key fallback. It should also honor the same SecretRef credential contract used by other web_search providers: configured env SecretRefs resolve to their referenced env value, and configured-but-unavailable SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently switching accounts.

## User Impact

Users who store the Gemini search API key as an env SecretRef now get the intended credential at request time. If that referenced secret is missing, Gemini web_search returns the existing missing-key diagnostic before any fetch is attempted instead of using another fallback key.

## Evidence

- Updated Gemini runtime credential resolution in `extensions/google/src/gemini-web-search-provider.runtime.ts`.
- Added focused regressions in `extensions/google/web-search-provider.test.ts` for:
  - configured Gemini env SecretRefs beating `GEMINI_API_KEY`
  - unavailable configured SecretRefs not falling back to env/provider credentials
  - Google model-provider env SecretRefs still working as fallback when no Gemini search key is configured

## Proof

- `OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=.vitest-cache-gemini-secretref node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/web-search-provider.test.ts`

target.title: fix(subagent): resolve runtime model from subagent default instead of parent primary
target.body:
## Summary

Two-part fix for subagent model resolution:

- **Commit 1 — read-side fallback (defense in depth, fbbd3c2d5f):** `resolveSessionModelRef` had no subagent awareness. When `entry.model` was empty (race between the spawn-side write and the gateway-side read at run-start), it fell through to `resolveDefaultModelForAgent`, returning the parent agent's primary model instead of the configured subagent default. Also reorders the `??` chain in `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection` so global `agents.defaults.subagents.model` takes precedence over the spawning agent's own `model` field.
- **Commit 2 — Pi-harness write-side fix (production path, this commit):** `getReplyFromConfig` resolved the run model via `resolveDefaultModel` (which goes through `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` and is not subagent-aware), and post-run persistence in `updateSessionStoreAfterAgentRun` then wrote that model back to `entry.model`, silently flipping every subagent run onto the parent agent's primary. The new `resolveSubagentSessionDefaultModel` helper performs a one-time override after `sessionEntry` is loaded so the Pi runtime boots on the configured subagent default and the post-run write preserves it.

## Failure mode (before)

Config:
```
agents.list[main].model.primary = anthropic/claude-opus-4-7
agents.defaults.subagents.model.primary = openai-codex/gpt-5.5
agents.list[main].subagents.model.primary = openai-codex/gpt-5.5
```

Spawn flow:
1. Parent calls `sessions_spawn(task=..., agentId=main)` with no explicit `model:`.
2. Spawn-side computes the right ref (`gpt-5.5`) and writes `entry.model` / `entry.modelProvider` via `persistInitialChildSessionRuntimeModel`.
3. The Pi runtime starts the run via `getReplyFromConfig`, which resolves `defaultProvider/defaultModel` via `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` — returning Opus (parent primary) — and uses that as the run's `provider/model`.
4. Subagent runs on Opus instead of gpt-5.5.
5. Post-run, `updateSessionStoreAfterAgentRun → setSessionRuntimeModel` writes Opus back to `entry.model`, clobbering the spawn-time gpt-5.5.

Result on disk: `~/.openclaw/agents/<agent>/sessions/sessions.json` shows `model: "claude-opus-4-7"` for entries with `subagentRole: "orchestrator", spawnDepth: 1`, even though `~/.openclaw/subagents/runs.json` correctly recorded `gpt-5.5`. The read-side fallback in commit 1 only kicks in while `entry.model` is empty — once the post-run write fires, `entry.model` is non-empty and the fallback is skipped.

## Fix

- **Commit 1 — `resolveSessionModelRef`:** when `entry.spawnDepth >= 1` or `entry.subagentRole` is set, fall back to the configured subagent default for this agent before falling through to the agent's primary.
- **Commit 1 — `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`:** reorder `??` chain to `agentConfig.subagents.model` → `agents.defaults.subagents.model` → `agentConfig.model`.
- **Commit 2 — `resolveSubagentSessionDefaultModel`:** new helper in `directive-handling.defaults.ts` that, given the loaded `sessionEntry`, checks the same subagent shape (`subagentRole` set or `spawnDepth >= 1`) and resolves the configured subagent default. `getReplyFromConfig` invokes it once after `sessionEntry` is loaded and overrides `defaultProvider/defaultModel/provider/model` so the Pi runtime boots and post-run-persists on the right model.

## Tests

- Read-side fallback tests in `src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts` cover the runtime subagent fallback (with and without `entry.spawnDepth`).
- Spawn-side chain-order tests cover the case where `agentConfig.subagents.model` is unset, `agents.defaults.subagents.model` is set, and `agentConfig.model` is set — we now return the global default instead of the agent's own primary.
- New tests in `src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.defaults.subagent.test.ts` cover the Pi-harness write-side helper: subagent sessions resolve to the configured subagent default; non-subagent sessions return null so the parent's primary is preserved.
- Existing get-reply test mocks updated to expose the new export.

## Scope

Commit 1: `src/gateway/session-utils.ts`, `src/agents/model-selection.ts`, and their tests.
Commit 2: `src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.defaults.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.ts`, and one new test plus two existing test-mock updates.
No drive-by changes.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Spawned subagent runs persisted the parent agent's primary model (e.g. `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7`) into `~/.openclaw/agents/<agent>/sessions/sessions.json` even though the configured subagent default was `openai-codex/gpt-5.5` and the spawn-side resolver had already written the correct ref. Subsequent turns then ran on the wrong model.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw install on macOS, Node 22, single-agent config with `agents.list[main].model.primary = anthropic/claude-opus-4-7`, `agents.defaults.subagents.model.primary = openai-codex/gpt-5.5`, and `agents.list[main].subagents.model.primary = openai-codex/gpt-5.5`. Subagent spawned via `sessions_spawn(task=..., agentId=main)` from a parent Telegram chat with no explicit `model:` argument.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. `pnpm openclaw doctor` to confirm config parses cleanly.
  2. Start gateway: `pnpm openclaw gateway start`.
  3. From the active chat, ask the agent to spawn a subagent with no model override.
  4. While the subagent is running and again after it completes, inspect `~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json` and `~/.openclaw/subagents/runs.json`.
- **Evidence after fix**: Inspected `~/.openclaw/agents/main/sessions/sessions.json` directly with `jq` — entries with `subagentRole: "orchestrator"` and `spawnDepth: 1` now persist `model: "gpt-5.5"` and `modelProvider: "openai-codex"` instead of `claude-opus-4-7`. `~/.openclaw/subagents/runs.json` continues to record `gpt-5.5` as before, and the gateway run trace prints the `openai-codex/gpt-5.5` provider/model pair when the run starts. Before the fix the same inspection printed `model: "claude-opus-4-7"` for those subagent entries even though the runs file recorded `gpt-5.5`.
- **Observed result after fix**: Subagent runs boot on `openai-codex/gpt-5.5` (visible in CLI run output and provider request logs), and the post-run write preserves that model in `sessions.json`, so subsequent turns of the same subagent session keep using `gpt-5.5`. Parent (non-subagent) sessions still resolve to `anthropic/claude-opus-4-7` as expected.
- **What was not tested**: Cross-agent configurations where the agent has no `subagents.model` and only `agents.defaults.subagents.model` is set were exercised only via the new unit tests, not on a live install. None of the alias-resolution paths were exercised against a real OpenRouter alias index live.

### Post-rebase verification (2026-05-12)

Rebase merged `upstream/main` (`e7e3e903bf`) into the branch and addressed the clawsweeper P2 finding on `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.ts:404-416`. Specifically: a spawned subagent child entry with no own `providerOverride`/`modelOverride` could still inherit the parent session's persisted `/model` override via `resolveStoredModelOverride` (parent-inheritance branch), silently flipping the run back to the parent's model. `resolveStoredModelOverride` now skips the parent-inheritance branch when the child entry is a subagent session (`subagentRole` set or `spawnDepth >= 1`). Direct child overrides and non-subagent (topic/thread) child sessions are unaffected. New regression coverage in `src/auto-reply/reply/stored-model-override.test.ts`.

- `pnpm tsgo` (core typecheck) -> exit 0, no diagnostics
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/stored-model-override.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/directive-handling.defaults.subagent.test.ts src/agents/model-selection.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts src/cron/isolated-agent.model-formatting.test.ts` -> 4 vitest shards passed (236 tests)
- `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply.block-streaming.test.ts` -> passed (1 test)
- `pnpm format:check` on touched files -> all clean after one auto-fix on `stored-model-override.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on touched files -> 0 warnings, 0 errors

target.body:
## Summary

- Rebases PR #94344 onto current main and resolves the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider conflicts without changing the intended SSRF contract.
- Updates the added SSRF tests to match the exported `LookupFn` overload shape.
- Updates the memory config docs to describe exact configured `baseUrl` hostname trust, not origin trust.
- Prevents configured local-service acquisition and health probes when the selected provider explicitly sets `request.allowPrivateNetwork: false`.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Operators using configured OpenAI-compatible memory embedding providers need the selected provider's private-endpoint policy to behave predictably: omitted policy preserves exact configured hostname compatibility, explicit `false` fails closed, and explicit `true` allows broader private-network access.
- **Scope boundary:** The rebase repair changes only the existing embedding SSRF policy integration, its tests/docs, and the local-service composition needed to honor explicit denial before any probe. It does not change schema, migrations, non-memory provider request paths, gateway/channel/session routing, global SSRF helpers, dependencies, or lockfiles.

Fixes #94166

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — existing PR author repair for #94344.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** #94180 (`feat(memory-core): allow private network endpoints for memory embeddings`). The public-contract helper also flagged #92307 through an environment/version term, but #92307 is about exec-approval startup warnings and is not the same embedding/private-network contract.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** #94180 adds a memory-specific config surface, `memorySearch.remote.network.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork`, for a trust decision that the selected model provider can already express with `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork`.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** This PR reuses the existing provider transport-trust contract as the canonical source of truth for configured providers instead of introducing a second memory-only knob. This update only repairs the review findings on that existing approach.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** The current-head bounded proof exercises the real `memory status --deep --json` CLI path against a loopback/private OpenAI-compatible daemon backed by the actual FastEmbed `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` model. Omitted policy succeeds through exact-hostname trust with one `/v1/embeddings` request, explicit `request.allowPrivateNetwork: false` is blocked before the daemon receives any request, and explicit `true` succeeds with one `/v1/embeddings` request.
- **Related open PR scan:** Current same-contract scan found #94180 as the linked alternative for memory private endpoint support; no broader canonical provider-inheritance PR was found besides this PR. #92307 was an environment/version false-positive and is not part of this embedding/private-network contract.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `openclaw memory status --deep` against a configured OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint on a loopback/private address must preserve exact-hostname compatibility when provider private-network policy is omitted, must block when the selected provider explicitly sets `request.allowPrivateNetwork: false`, and must honor `request.allowPrivateNetwork: true` for explicit broader private-network trust.
- **Canonical reachability path:** User `models.providers.<id>` and `agents.defaults.memorySearch` config → existing config schema/type parsing and configured-provider normalization → `ConfiguredEmbeddingProvider.request.allowPrivateNetwork` on the runtime embedding client → shared SSRF policy → guarded `/v1/embeddings` request or pre-request block.
- **Boundary crossed:** Full config-to-request local runtime path through the real `openclaw memory status --deep --json` CLI and `memory-core` embedding probe into a real FastEmbed model daemon. This is local-daemon behavior proof, not third-party provider proof.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused the repository shared `ssrfPolicyFromHttpBaseUrlAllowedHostname` helper and `resolvePinnedHostnameWithPolicy` test seam. No numeric-string parser or provider-owned range constraint is added or changed; the only provider contract consumed is the existing boolean `request.allowPrivateNetwork` setting.
- **Real environment tested:** CLI behavior proof was captured in the local PR worktree on Linux, using the real source CLI, the real `memory-core` CLI command, isolated `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and an OpenAI-compatible FastEmbed `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` daemon bound to a loopback/private address. The proof is bound to current HEAD by daily-fix's non-mock live-proof receipt. Current-head re-verification also covered the rebased runtime integration, test typing, docs wording, and the explicit-denial plus configured-local-service combination.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** The live runtime proof command used for the PR behavior was:

```sh
node scripts/run-node.mjs memory status --agent proof --deep --json
```

The current rebased head was re-verified with these commands from `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-94344`:

```sh
pnpm exec tsc --ignoreConfig --strict --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext --target ES2022 --types node --noEmit /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-94344-evidence/lookupfn-overload-smoke.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts
pnpm check:test-types
git diff --check
```

- **Evidence after fix:** Exact-hostname compatibility result from the real CLI, with provider `request.allowPrivateNetwork` omitted:

```json
{
  "agentId": "proof",
  "status": {
    "provider": "openai-compatible",
    "requestedProvider": "private-embedding-proof",

}
```

```json
}
```

Explicit provider denial result from the real CLI:

```json

  "status": {
    "provider": "openai-compatible",
    "requestedProvider": "private-embedding-proof",
    "model": "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5"
  },
  "embeddingProbe": {
    "ok": false,
    "error": "Blocked hostname or private/internal/special-use IP address"
  }
}
```

Explicit provider denial summary:

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "containsGuardBlock": true,
  "containsEmbeddingsReady": false,
  "serverRequestCount": 0
}
```

Provider opt-in overlay result from the real CLI:

```json

  "agentId": "proof",
  "status": {

}
```

```json

}
```

Bound current-head daemon proof summary:

```json
{
  "head": "7f3916ffca66cfab7ecd7d19ee5e6a746b126d86",
  "target": "FastEmbed BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 local embedding daemon",
  "omitted": { "code": 0, "ready": true, "request_count": 1 },
  "explicit_false": { "code": 0, "ready": false, "blocked": true, "request_count": 0 },
  "explicit_true": { "code": 0, "ready": true, "request_count": 1 },
  "embedding_dimension": 384,
  "passed": true
}
```

Current-head review repair verification:

```text
LookupFn overload smoke: passed with no TypeScript diagnostics.
openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts: Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 35 passed (35), including configured localService plus explicit private-network denial.
pnpm check:test-types: completed with exit code 0 after rebase; after the final localService denial guard, fresh `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both exited 0.
git diff --check: passed.
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The omitted configured provider alias reaches the loopback/private embedding endpoint successfully. The explicit false config is blocked by the guarded-fetch path before the endpoint sees a request. The explicit true config returns `embeddingProbe.ok: true` and reaches the endpoint once. The current update also resolves the `LookupFn` overload type issue and keeps the provider test passing under the owning Vitest config.
- **What was not tested:** I did not use a maintainer's real private LAN/VPN embedding service, third-party credentials, Mantis, Telegram, or Desktop proof infrastructure. This PR does not touch Telegram/Desktop/channel delivery; the local proof exercises the relevant memory CLI, configured-provider, and guarded-fetch runtime surface. I did not drive a live metadata/link-local endpoint for safety; metadata/link-local rebinding remains covered by the regression test that resolves an exact-hostname policy to `169.254.169.254` and expects private/internal blocking when broader opt-in is not set. I did not run `openclaw memory index --force`; `memory status --deep` is the requested memory runtime probe path and reaches the embedding availability check directly.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix plus author-side review repair.

## Review findings addressed

| Finding | Status | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RF-001 | Addressed | This author update responds to the current `status: ⏳ waiting on author` state. Label removal still depends on the next ClawSweeper/maintainer pass after submission. |
| RF-002 | Disclosed/maintainer decision | Explicit `request.allowPrivateNetwork: false` intentionally fails closed for configured private endpoints that previously depended on omitted-policy exact-hostname trust. The docs and three-state proof make that upgrade-sensitive behavior explicit rather than silently preserving unsafe compatibility. |
| RF-003 | Disclosed/maintainer decision | The omitted/false/true SSRF contract remains a maintainer/security-boundary decision. This contributor update implements and proves the requested behavior but does not present that policy choice as independently approved. |
| RF-004 | Fixed within scope / disclosed | Fresh isolated configs were exercised for omitted, explicit false, and explicit true. The resolver repair consumes only canonical private-network posture fields; existing embedding base URL, header, API-key, proxy, and TLS construction is unchanged. A real upgrade from a maintainer deployment with custom auth/proxy/TLS was not exercised and remains disclosed below. |
| RF-005 | Fixed/proven | Replaced the adapter-local private-network decision with `resolveProviderRequestPolicyConfig`, then repeated the full three-state CLI proof against the real FastEmbed daemon. |
| RF-006 | Fixed/proven | The embedding client now calls the canonical provider request resolver with provider id, API, normalized base URL, `capability: "other"`, `transport: "http"`, and the configured request posture. A failing-first integration test locks that call. |
| RF-007 | Fixed/proven | `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts src/agents/provider-request-config.test.ts` passed; the provider suite reports 36/36 tests. |
| RF-008 | Fixed/proven | `pnpm check:test-types` completed successfully across core-test, extensions-test, and test-root. |
| RF-009 | Fixed/proven | `git diff --check` completed with no output, and oxfmt reports both changed TypeScript files correctly formatted. |
| RF-010 | Fixed/proven | Repeated the requested redacted `memory status --agent proof --deep --json` runtime proof for all three policy states against the real FastEmbed model daemon: omitted succeeded with one embedding POST, explicit `false` was blocked with zero health probes and zero embedding POSTs, and explicit `true` succeeded with one embedding POST. The bound summary is `live-proof/fastembed-current-head.json`, with its daily-fix live-proof receipt alongside it. |

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts`
- **Target files:** `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts`; `docs/reference/memory-config.md`
- **Scenario locked in:** Configured OpenAI-compatible memory providers use the selected provider request policy: omitted policy keeps exact configured `baseUrl` hostname trust, explicit `false` opts out of exact-hostname private-network trust, and explicit `true` allows broader private-network embedding requests. The test fixtures also keep private/internal resolution blocked when broader opt-in is not set.
- **Commands run after this author repair:**

```sh
pnpm exec tsc --ignoreConfig --strict --module NodeNext --moduleResolution NodeNext --target ES2022 --types node --noEmit /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-94344-evidence/lookupfn-overload-smoke.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts
pnpm check:test-types
git diff --check
```

- **Observed local result:** The `LookupFn` overload smoke passed without TypeScript diagnostics; `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts` passed 35/35 tests under `test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts`; full post-rebase `pnpm check:test-types` exited 0, then fresh `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both exited 0 after the final localService denial guard; `git diff --check` exited 0.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The rebase keeps the existing provider-policy helper and adds one composition guard so explicit denial is enforced before local-service acquisition. The owning provider test locks the combined path without expanding unrelated provider or gateway coverage.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** security-boundary, compatibility, auth-provider.
- **Risk explanation:** The PR touches the security boundary for private-network embedding fetches and the provider/config contract that decides when exact-hostname or broader private-network trust is allowed. A wrong change could relax SSRF blocking by default, break existing configured local/private aliases, or create a second incompatible memory-only trust surface.
- **Why acceptable:** The PR's runtime behavior remains constrained to the OpenAI-compatible embedding provider policy: omitted config preserves exact configured hostname trust, explicit false denies exact-hostname private trust and now also prevents local-service probes, and explicit true is required for broader private-network access.
- **What did NOT change:** No schema, migration, new config key, provider parser/range, global SSRF helper, non-memory provider transport, gateway/channel/session routing, dependency, lockfile, or unrelated cleanup changed. The test-only `as unknown as` casts adapt partial config and overloaded `LookupFn` fixtures; the canonical config-to-request reachability is separately exercised through the real CLI path above.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The original issue is that memory-core OpenAI-compatible embeddings did not consistently consume the selected configured provider's `request.allowPrivateNetwork` policy when building the embedding SSRF policy. During rebase, current main's configured local-service acquisition path composed ahead of guarded fetch, so explicit denial could still trigger a private health probe before the embedding POST was blocked. The adapter also continued reading the boolean directly after current main introduced the canonical provider request resolver, creating a second policy decision path.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The embedding client now obtains `allowPrivateNetwork` and `privateNetworkExplicitlyDenied` from `resolveProviderRequestPolicyConfig`, uses that one result for both SSRF policy and local-service acquisition, and preserves existing header/auth/base URL construction. It does not add downstream fetch fallbacks, a parallel memory-only knob, or unrelated runtime changes.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix with focused author repair.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The canonical contract surface is `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork` for configured provider transport trust. Memory embedding SSRF policy consumes that provider-owned request setting; this PR does not add a parallel `memorySearch` private-network knob, does not change schema/default values, and does not alter unrelated provider, gateway, channel, or session contracts.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** Medium-high — local CLI proof exists for the runtime path, the current author repair passes focused and full test-type verification, and the remaining SSRF/private-network acceptance is disclosed as maintainer/security judgment rather than presented as already externally approved.
- **Patch quality notes:** The `as unknown as LookupFn` casts are test-only fixtures for the overloaded `dns.promises.lookup` signature and match the existing SSRF pinning test pattern; the `EmbeddingProviderCreateOptions["config"]` casts are partial canonical config fixtures, not production type suppression. The runtime `return undefined` for explicit false is the intentional provider-denial path, and the local-service guard prevents any pre-guard probe under that same canonical config. No skipped tests, `.only`, lint disables, runtime catch-all fallback, schema migration, or new public config knob were added.

target.title: fix(telegram): prevent unlisted API calls from stalling delivery
target.body:
Closes #104524

AI-assisted: yes. I used an OpenAI coding agent, reviewed the resulting change, and understand the timeout behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram users could have all outbound replies for a session stall for roughly eight minutes when an API call used a method that was not explicitly listed in the client timeout table.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every identified Telegram API method except `getUpdates` now receives the existing 60-second outbound timeout as a default. Explicit method-specific guards remain unchanged, higher configured timeouts are still honored, and requests whose method cannot be identified remain untouched.

## User Impact

A newly introduced or otherwise unlisted Telegram API method can no longer silently fall back to grammY's approximately 500-second timeout and park the serialized delivery lane. Its client-side guard defaults to 60 seconds unless the operator configured a higher timeout.

## Evidence

- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts` — 1 file, 15 tests passed.
- `pnpm test:extension telegram` — 142 files, 2,666 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.ts extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.ts extensions/telegram/src/request-timeouts.test.ts` — formatting passed.
- `NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=2300' node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/telegram/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

No live Telegram probe was run because this checkout has no test-bot credentials. The linked issue includes the production incident evidence and reports the same fallback behavior running in production.

### Controlled runtime proof

A credential-free controlled Bot API endpoint exercised the real `createTelegramClientFetch` and `AbortController` path on this PR branch. All three requests ran concurrently against delayed local HTTP responses; no Telegram token or external API was used.

```text
controlled_endpoint=http://127.0.0.1:<redacted>/bot<redacted>/METHOD
unlisted-default: answerCallbackQuery, server delay 65000ms -> aborted after 60004ms: Telegram answercallbackquery timed out after 60000ms
unlisted-configured-override: answerCallbackQuery, configured timeout 70s, server delay 62000ms -> HTTP 200 after 62030ms
getUpdates-unchanged: getUpdates, configured timeout 70s, server delay 65000ms -> aborted after 45015ms: Telegram getupdates timed out after 45000ms
proof_result=PASS
```

This demonstrates the 60-second fallback through the actual fetch wrapper, the existing higher configured-timeout escape hatch, and the unchanged 45-second `getUpdates` guard.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(media): bound hung remote downloads in media store
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users and gateway paths that persist remote media through `saveMediaSource()` would hang indefinitely when a media URL accepted the TCP connection but never sent response headers, or sent a partial body and then stalled. Only a max-bytes cap existed; there was no header or idle-read timeout, so requests, temp files, and caller chains could stay pinned forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add 30s response-header and idle-body timeouts to `downloadToFile()` in the media store path, matching the hang-bounding intent already used by `src/media/fetch.ts` / web-media reads. On failure, abort the request/response/write stream, await pipeline shutdown, then remove the temp file before rejecting—so platforms that reject unlinking an open file cannot retain partial media.

This path stays local to `saveMediaSource()` because that caller streams into a sibling temp file while sniffing MIME; `saveRemoteMedia()` / fetch.ts does not own that contract. Shared outcome is the same hang bound, not a duplicated fetch stack.

Timeouts are overridable in tests via `setMediaStoreNetworkDepsForTest`. MIME sniffing, redirect header stripping, and the 5MB size cap stay unchanged.

## User Impact

**Before:** A hung or adversarial media URL could block `saveMediaSource()` (including gateway managed-image ingestion) with no recovery besides process restart, and failure cleanup could race stream close.

**After:** Stalled header waits and idle body reads fail within 30s; streams close before temp removal; callers get a clear timeout/stall error with no leftover media files.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/media/store.ts` (`downloadToFile`)
- Caller under test: production `saveMediaSource(httpUrl)` against a real local `node:http` server
- Regression: `src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts`
- Sibling redirect suite still green: `src/media/store.redirect.test.ts`

### Unit regression

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts src/media/store.redirect.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text

 ✓ |media| src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts > media store download timeouts > times out when the response body stalls after partial data 45ms
 ✓ |media| src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts > media store download timeouts > still saves when the remote body completes before idle timeout 12ms
 ✓ |media| src/media/store.redirect.test.ts > media store redirects > follows redirects and keeps detected mime/extension 31ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 3.98s
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `saveMediaSource()` remote downloads no longer hang forever on servers that accept connections without sending headers, or that stall after partial body data; temp files are cleaned up only after stream teardown.
- **Canonical reachability path:** gateway/managed-image and other callers → `saveMediaSource(url)` → `downloadToFile()` → header timer / idle body timer → abort streams → await pipeline → temp cleanup → reject.
- **Boundary crossed:** Untrusted remote HTTP(S) media source → local media-store temp file / saved media ID.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Aligns store downloads with media `fetch.ts` / web-media header + idle-read hang bounds. Keeps store-local downloader because `saveMediaSource()` needs sniff-while-streaming into a sibling temp file that `saveRemoteMedia()` does not provide. SSRF pinned-hostname lookup and redirect header stripping unchanged.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Node source checkout; standalone `tsx` script (outside Vitest) calling production `saveMediaSource` against a real `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1` with pinned loopback lookup.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/media/store.download-timeout.test.ts src/media/store.redirect.test.ts --reporter=verbose
# plus standalone tsx proof invoking saveMediaSource() against hung sockets
```

```text

hang-headers: Media download timed out waiting for response headers after 80ms
hang-headers leftover files: []
stall-body: rejected after 85ms
stall-body: Media download stalled: no data received for 80ms
stall-body leftover files: []
standalone-proof: done

 ✓ ... > times out when the server accepts a connection but never sends headers 52ms

```

- **Observed result after fix:** Hang-headers and stall-body both reject with explicit timeout/stall errors; both leave zero files under the media root. Successful short responses still save. Lint clean on touched files.

target.title: fix(crabbox): preserve UTF-16 boundaries in CLI failure detail truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Crabbox worker error details contain malformed text when a command's stderr has emoji at the 512-character truncation boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

`commandDetail()` replaced raw `.slice(0, MAX_ERROR_DETAIL_CHARS)` with the shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper from the public plugin SDK barrel. The `.replace(/\s+/gu, " ")` whitespace compression runs before truncation, making the content more dense — which increases the likelihood that non-ASCII characters (emoji in test output, script diagnostics) land on the 512 boundary. The existing code-unit limit and message format remain unchanged; this only backs a cut up to avoid splitting an emoji surrogate pair.

## User Impact

Crabbox worker CLI error messages (warmup/inspect/stop failures) remain well-formed when the remote command output contains long emoji-containing diagnostic text.

## Evidence

### Provider-path regression test (exercises real `provider.inspect()` → `commandError()` → `commandDetail()`)

The new test constructs 511 ASCII `x` chars + `😀after` in stderr and calls `provider.inspect()` with a mock CLI runner returning exit code 2. The full chain is: `provider.inspect()` → `inspectWithContext()` → `commandError("inspect", result)` → `commandDetail(result)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(compressed, 512)`. Current main's raw `.slice(0, 512)` splits the surrogate pair; the fix backs up to 511, preserving well-formed UTF-16.

### Direct-formatter regression test (exercises real `testing.commandDetail()`)

Same boundary construction (511 ASCII + emoji) but calls `commandDetail()` directly for focused coverage of the truncation path. Both tests complement each other — the provider-path test proves the real scenario, the direct test catches regressions at the narrowest boundary.

### Terminal behavior proof (before vs. after, live Node.js output)

```
=== PR #104612 Live Terminal Proof ===

Input: 511 'x' + emoji + 'after'
  stderr[511]=0xd83d (HIGH surrogate)
  stderr[512]=0xde00 (LOW surrogate)

--- BEFORE fix (current main) ---
  output: ": x...x\ud83d"
  length: 514 code units
  LONE SURROGATE at index 513: 0xd83d ← MALFORMED

--- AFTER fix (truncateUtf16Safe) ---
  output: ": x...x"
  length: 513 code units
  ✅ No lone surrogates — well-formed UTF-16
```

### Test suite
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.test.ts -t "preserves well-formed UTF-16"
 ✓ |extensions| crabbox-worker-provider.test.ts > Crabbox worker provider > preserves well-formed UTF-16 through the provider boundary when inspect stderr crosses the truncation limit 63ms
 ✓ |extensions| crabbox-worker-provider.test.ts > Crabbox worker provider > preserves well-formed UTF-16 when CLI failure detail reaches the boundary limit 4ms

      Tests  2 passed | 45 skipped (47)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-provider.test.ts
 ✓ 47/47 passed
```

### Lint
```

✓ clean
```

target.body:
Closes [#89200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89200)

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and tests were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment's session store.

## What Problem This Solves

Session trajectory artifacts (`.trajectory.jsonl` + `.trajectory-path.json`) were handled inconsistently, and destructively, across the session lifecycle:

1. **Delete** (dashboard / `sessions.delete` RPC) archived the transcript but left the trajectory pair orphaned on disk forever (the original [#89200](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89200) defect).
2. **Reset paths** either deleted the trajectory outright (destroying the forensic tool-call record, flagged as a P1 by the automated review on this PR) or left it at its live name to be misclassified later.
3. The **typed `/new` and `/reset`** commands (and the implicit daily/idle rollover) went through a code path with no trajectory handling at all, so fixes applied to the other reset doors never reached the path users actually type.

## What This Change Does

One consistent model: **trajectory artifacts shadow their transcript**. Whenever a session's transcript is archived with a `.reset.<ts>` or `.deleted.<ts>` suffix, the trajectory runtime file and pointer are renamed with the byte-identical suffix in the same operation (shared `nowMs`), never unlinked:

- A `TrajectoryArtifactDisposal` union threads the disposal mode through the cleanup helpers: `{ mode: "tombstone", reason, nowMs }` for user-visible lifecycle events, with rename-in-place semantics under the same `withTrajectoryPathLock` retire turn.
- All three lifecycle doors are coupled: `deleteSessionEntryLifecycle` (delete), `resetSessionEntryLifecycle` (dashboard New Session button), and the typed-command rollover path `initSessionState` → `commitReplySessionInitialization`, plus the internal self-heal path `persistSessionResetLifecycle`.
- The referenced-sessions guard snapshot is taken **inside the locked store mutator** (`referencedSessionIdsAtSwap`), closing a race where an unlocked re-read after two await points could see a concurrent writer's row and silently skip the tombstone.
- **External trajectory directories** (`OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR`): the pair is tombstoned in place only under proven ownership (registry-owned, or the session's own pointer file names the target); unproven files in an operator-configured directory are left untouched. The retention sweep follows tombstone directories, so aging works there too.
- **No new retention code.** Tombstoned trajectories reuse the existing `.reset.<ts>` / `.deleted.<ts>` suffix conventions and age out with the existing archived-transcript sweep.

## Why rename instead of delete on reset

No merged commit or confirmed-maintainer comment currently states reset-vs-trajectory policy explicitly, but the record strongly and repeatedly converges on one answer: reset must preserve trajectory records via rename/archive, never delete them outright. This is proposed directly in [#90707](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90707) (with a concrete forensics-loss incident as motivation), implemented the same way in the still-open [#94593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593) (after two prior closed-unmerged attempts at the identical shape, [#93319](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/93319) and [#94895](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94895)), echoed by the broader "never `rm` a session file, only move/rename" position in [#56609](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/56609), and most directly, flagged as a P1 blocker on this very branch by the automated reviewer, which asked explicitly to "preserve or archive pre-reset trajectories instead of deleting them." This PR's tombstone-rename on the runner-driven `/reset` path is our attempt to satisfy that converging intent without waiting on #94593 to land, since the two changes touch adjacent but distinct code paths (delete-lifecycle cleanup vs. the shared reset-archive helper) and reconciling them is better done as a maintainer-guided follow-up than by blocking this fix on an unrelated open PR.

## Evidence

Test gates on the final head: `session-accessor.test.ts` 73/73, `session.test.ts` 143/143, adjacent lifecycle suites 24/24 (240 total), typecheck (`tsgo:core` + `tsgo:core:test`) clean, oxlint/oxfmt clean. Every fix commit is red-proven: the concurrent-writer race test and the entry-level typed-`/reset` test (entering through `initSessionState`, not the inner function) each fail against the pre-fix code exactly as observed live and pass after.

Live validation on a v2026.6.10 production deployment (session ids redacted):

```
typed /reset:
  <sid-A>.jsonl.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z
  <sid-A>.trajectory.jsonl.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z
  <sid-A>.trajectory-path.json.reset.2026-07-11T16-45-15.346Z

dashboard delete: same trio shape with .deleted.<ts>, session key removed, clean re-mint on next message

typed /new with OPENCLAW_TRAJECTORY_DIR set (trajectory lives outside the sessions dir):
  sessions dir:  <sid-B>.jsonl.reset.<ts>  +  <sid-B>.trajectory-path.json.reset.<ts>
  external dir:  <sid-B>.jsonl.reset.<ts>   (renamed in place, same timestamp)
```

## Scope notes

- `applySessionEntryLifecycleMutation` (the batched background-maintenance mutation used by the session reaper, cleanup service, and heartbeat runner) is deliberately not touched: its removed-session cleanup already routes through the trajectory-coupled maintenance helpers, and unreferenced pairs are reclaimed by the age-based prune, which is the correct model for background reaping (no user action to timestamp-couple to).
- [#94593](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94593) partially overlaps on intent (reset-time preservation) but implements it in the shared reset-archive helper; this PR covers the delete lifecycle and the typed-command rollover door. If #94593 lands first we are happy to rebase and drop any overlap, and vice versa.

## User Impact

Deleting or resetting a session, from any surface, now leaves a complete archived trio with one shared timestamp instead of orphaned or destroyed trajectory files. Post-incident forensics of tool calls survives resets. Existing retention behavior and bounds are unchanged.

target.title: fix(clawrouter): guard usage snapshot fetch against SSRF redirects
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where ClawRouter usage snapshot fetches used an unguarded `fetch` against an operator-configured `baseUrl`. A malicious or compromised usage endpoint could redirect the request onto a private/internal address, and the call path skipped the shared SSRF guard already used for ClawRouter live catalog discovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Route `fetchClawRouterUsage` through `fetchWithSsrFGuard` the same way live catalog discovery does: the guard owns production transport (no caller `fetchImpl`), so DNS pinning cannot be overwritten by provider usage proxy wrappers. Tests inject an optional `fetchGuard` seam; production callers no longer pass `ctx.fetchFn`.

## User Impact

ClawRouter `/usage` status no longer follows redirects from the configured host into private/internal networks. Healthy public ClawRouter usage endpoints continue to work.

## Evidence

### Unit + controlled-server production-transport proof

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ ... > maps the managed monthly budget and usage totals 151ms
 ✓ ... > shows aggregate usage for an unmetered key 2ms
 ✓ ... > does not expose an upstream error body 1ms
 ✓ ... > bounds successful usage response bodies 17ms
 ✓ ... > fetches usage through the production SSRF-guarded transport 326ms
 ✓ ... > blocks private-network redirects on the production transport path 55ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.62s
```

The last two cases exercise production `fetchClawRouterUsage` with no injected fetch/guard: a real `node:http` loopback server for healthy usage, and a `302` to `http://10.0.0.1:9/v1/usage` that the shared guard rejects before a second hop.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** ClawRouter usage fetches no longer follow redirects from the configured host onto private/internal targets, and production transport stays under the shared SSRF guard's dispatcher.
- **Canonical reachability path:** provider usage snapshot → `fetchUsageSnapshot` in `extensions/clawrouter/index.ts` → `fetchClawRouterUsage` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` (no `fetchImpl`).
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime SSRF guard; controlled `node:http` server on loopback; private redirect target.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `fetchWithSsrFGuard` + `ssrfPolicyFromHttpBaseUrlAllowedHostname` already used by ClawRouter live catalog discovery; same guard-owned transport shape as catalog (no provider usage proxy as `fetchImpl`).
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with real HTTP listeners.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
 ✓ |extensions| extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts > ClawRouter usage > fetches usage through the production SSRF-guarded transport 326ms
 ✓ |extensions| extensions/clawrouter/usage.test.ts > ClawRouter usage > blocks private-network redirects on the production transport path 55ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 5.62s
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Healthy usage returns the mapped snapshot over the guard-owned transport; private-network redirect rejects with a blocked/private/internal error and the controlled server sees only the first hop.
- **What was not tested:** Live ClawRouter cloud `/v1/usage` against a real proxy key; Gateway status UI end-to-end; HTTP_PROXY-managed usage routing (usage now matches catalog and uses guard-owned direct transport rather than `resolveProxyFetchFromEnv` as `fetchImpl`).
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. Only the ClawRouter usage HTTP transport gains the shared SSRF guard with guard-owned dispatcher. Successful responses from the configured host are unchanged; operator-configured private base URLs remain allowed when that hostname is the configured endpoint (same policy shape as catalog discovery). Usage snapshot fetching no longer routes through the provider usage proxy fetch wrapper, matching catalog discovery.

target.body:
Closes #103758

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where LINE groups configured with `requireMention: true` could not require a mention before non-text messages (image/video/audio/file) reached the agent. Any photo, video, voice clip, or file posted in such a group was always processed, regardless of whether the bot was actually mentioned, because LINE's Messaging API never attaches mention metadata to non-text messages and the mention-gate logic could not account for that.

Fixes an issue where operators of mention-gated LINE groups would see the bot react to every image/video/audio/file dropped in the chat, even when nobody addressed the bot, when they expected the same "must be mentioned" behavior that already applies to text messages (per #34438 / #35847).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds two new **opt-in** LINE group config fields — `requireMentionForNonText` and `pendingMediaLimit` — so operators can explicitly turn on mention gating for non-text messages without changing default behavior for anyone else. Because LINE never reports a mention on the non-text message itself, a bounded per-group pending-media queue (default limit 3) retains the most recent skipped media until a later message in the same group is mentioned and fully processed, at which point the queued media is attached to that turn and the queue is cleared. This lets a user post a photo, then follow up with `@bot look at this`, and have the photo still reach the agent.

A prior attempt at the opt-in flag alone (#68197) went stale without merging and did not include the retention queue, which meant skipped media was simply dropped forever once a group opted in — this PR keeps the same opt-in, default-false posture that maintainers asked for on #68197, and adds the missing retention piece on top.

## User Impact

LINE operators can now set `channels.line.accounts.<id>.groups.<groupId>.requireMentionForNonText: true` (alongside `requireMention: true`) to require an `@mention` before non-text messages reach the agent, matching the existing text-message behavior. Skipped media isn't lost — up to `pendingMediaLimit` (default 3) recent items are retained per group and delivered alongside the next mentioned message. Existing configs are unaffected since both fields default to off/unset.

## Evidence

`pnpm test:extension line` — 26 test files, **313 tests passing** (up from 307 on `main`; +6 in `bot-handlers.test.ts`, +2 in `config-schema.test.ts`):

```

```

New tests cover:

- unmentioned non-text message is skipped when `requireMentionForNonText` is set (and the pre-existing "allows non-text through by default" test is preserved unchanged, proving no default-behavior change);
- pending-queue eviction bounded by `pendingMediaLimit` (oldest dropped first);
- queued media flushed into `allMedia`/`processMessage` context on a later mentioned message, then the queue is cleared;
- default `pendingMediaLimit` of 3 when unset;
- schema acceptance of both new fields and rejection of non-positive `pendingMediaLimit`.
